## Goal

Make "won a game" a first-class, engine-generic achievement event so the give-away triggers have a real, Steam-free source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AchievementSystem` (or a documented thin extension) gains an idempotent game-outcome surface (e.g. `onGameOutcome({ gameId, outcome })`) that unlocks mapped achievements via the existing `AchievementSink`; zero Steam/Electron imports.
- The launcher manifest defines `first-win` and `second-distinct-game-win` meta-achievements (titles, descriptions, hidden flags) and the outcome-to-achievement mapping is engine-generic.
- "Second distinct game" logic only unlocks after wins in two different game ids; re-wins of the same game do not.
- `SteamAchievementService` idempotence and offline paths are reused unchanged for the meta-achievements.
- Unit tests cover outcome-to-unlock, distinct-game counting, idempotence, and no-op for unknown outcomes; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `electron/achievement-manifest.json`
- `tests/steam-achievements/achievement-outcome.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Engine outcome surface, manifest meta-achievements, unit tests.
data.title: Engine game-outcome surface and cross-game meta-achievements

data.description:
# Goal

As a game developer depending on the engine, I want a core-owned, exported
renderer-aware container clip so a WebGL boot clips panel content exactly like a
Canvas boot does — and downstream repos stop carrying their own copies.

Port the proven pattern from `../tce-main-street/src/ContainerClip.ts`
(do **not** re-invent it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Core helper.** A renderer-aware container-clip helper exists in core, exported
  through the public `@ui` surface with the `ContainerClip` API (`setRect`,
  `clear`, `destroy`) and the Canvas/WebGL branching described below.
- **WebGL browser test.** At least one browser test forces `Phaser.WEBGL` and
  asserts clipping actually happens (pixel probe via `renderer.snapshotPixel()`)
  and that no `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warning is emitted from core
  code; Canvas parity is asserted in the same file.
- `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts` exports `createContainerClip(scene, target, rect?)`
  and the `ContainerClip` interface (`renderer`, `graphics`, `geometryMask`,
  `maskFilter`, `rect`, `active`, `setRect`, `clear`, `destroy`), plus
  `isWebGLRenderer(scene)`; both are exported from `src/ui/index.ts` so
  downstream repos import them from `@ui`.
- Canvas branch keeps today's behaviour: transparent-fill `GeometryMask`,
  Graphics on the display list, `clearMask()` on `clear()` — Canvas rendering
  output is unchanged.
- WebGL branch: `target.enableFilters()` then
  `target.filters.internal.addMask(graphics, false, scene.cameras.main)`; the
  mask Graphics is created with `scene.make.graphics(..., false)` (**off** the
  display list) and drawn **opaque**; a missing filter list (no WebGL context)
  degrades to `maskFilter === null` without throwing.
- `clear()` is a real "no clip" on both renderers, and `destroy()` is
  idempotent and removes the filter / mask resources.
- The module doc comment records the Phaser 4 (`4.0.0-rc.7`) restriction —
  `GameObject.setMask` logs "not supported in WebGL" and no-ops — and why the
  mask must be opaque and off the display list.
- Unit tests (`tests/ui/ContainerClip.test.ts`) cover renderer branch selection,
  `clear()`/`destroy()` idempotence and post-destroy no-ops, using stubs.
- Browser test (`tests/ui/ContainerClip.browser.test.ts`), written **before**
  the helper (TDD): under `Phaser.WEBGL` a clipped container's content is
  visible inside the rect and absent outside it (`renderer.snapshotPixel()`
  probe), the result is unchanged when the container is translated (screen-space
  mask), **and no** `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warning is captured;
  the same file asserts Canvas parity (clip applied via `GeometryMask`).

## Key Files

- `src/ui/ContainerClip.ts`
- `src/ui/index.ts`
- `tests/ui/ContainerClip.test.ts`
- `tests/ui/ContainerClip.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/helpers/bootRendererScene.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked-by `CG-0MVTQ3UFI009LH8Q` (WebGL clip test harness).

## Deliverables

- Helper + exports + unit tests + WebGL/Canvas browser parity test green;
  `npm run build` green.
data.title: Core ContainerClip helper: renderer-aware clipping exported from @ui

data.description:
## Goal

Render each buffered game event as a one-line header plus fully pretty-printed, unwrapped payload inside the Game Events debug overlay, and keep wide lines reachable with the new opt-in horizontal scroll — the user-visible end of the change.

## Scope

- `src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts`:
  - Delete `truncatePayload`; render `formatEventLogEntry(entry)` from the sibling formatter module.
  - One `scene.add.text` per **event** (not per JSON line) at a measured y offset, with `lineSpacing`, `fontSize: '13px'`, `fontFamily: overlay.monoFont`, and **no** `wordWrap`.
  - Track the maximum `textObj.width` (and the tallest text height) as objects are created, then call `overlay.refresh(totalHeight, totalWidth)` so the dialog clamps both axes; event count per buffer update is unchanged (poll path untouched).
  - Request `enableHorizontalScroll: true` on `createOverlayDialog` for this overlay only.
  - Keep the status/`countText`/Clear/Pause-Resume controls, the `hudContainer` parenting, the 500 ms poll, the empty-state text and the close/cleanup path exactly as today; add a short hint to the status line that wide payloads scroll horizontally.
- New `tests/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.browser.test.ts` (browser project, real Phaser CANVAS scene): subscribe `GlobalEventBuffer` to a real `GameEventEmitter`, emit an event with a nested payload, activate the tool, then assert:
  - the rendered text contains the pretty-printed body and spans multiple lines;
  - the text objects have no `wordWrap` width set;
  - `refresh` was given a content height that grows with the payload line count (or the returned handle's clamp allows the taller content);
  - an event whose payload is circular still renders and does not block the other events.
- Write the browser test first (TDD red inside this item), then implement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Full payload pretty-printed: each buffered event's payload is rendered as indented multi-line JSON under a one-line `timestamp [eventName]` header, and the 80-character truncation is removed so the entire payload appears with no silent data loss.
- [ ] No horizontal soft-wrapping: payload lines are never word-wrapped, and each pretty-printed JSON line is rendered as exactly one line with no `wordWrap` on the text objects.
- [ ] Nothing is hidden at the right edge: lines wider than the dialog's content area are fully reachable through the opt-in horizontal scrolling this overlay requests, while vertical scrolling and `refresh(totalContentHeight)` clamping keep working.
- [ ] Non-serialisable payloads degrade safely: `undefined`, `null`, primitives and circular structures render without throwing, and a circular payload does not break rendering of the remaining events.
- [ ] Existing overlay behaviour is preserved: Clear, Pause/Resume, the 500 ms poll, the event count, the buffer-status text, the `hudContainer` parenting and the close/cleanup path all behave as they do today.
- [ ] A browser test (or an equivalent deterministic Phaser-level test) verifies the rendered result: multi-line text present, no wrap configured, and the scroll content height grows with the payload line count.
- [ ] Build and targeted suites pass: `npm run build` succeeds and the unit and browser suites covering `src/ui/debug` pass (run through the test skill).
- [ ] Code comments/JSDoc document the row layout (header + body, one object per event) and the horizontal-scroll hint.

## Verification

- `/skill:test --type unit` and `/skill:test --type browser` (never run `vitest` directly).
- `npm run build`.

## Key Files

- `src/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.ts`
- `tests/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.browser.test.ts`
- `src/ui/debug/formatEventLog.ts`
- `src/ui/Overlay.ts`

**Parent:** CG-0MVTTR0OC006PWDK — AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7
data.title: Pretty-print payloads in Game Events overlay

data.author: Map
data.comment: TDD inside this item: `tests/ui/debug/GameEventLogOverlay.browser.test.ts` was authored first and verified red against the old renderer — single-line raw JSON (`timestamp [name] {...}`), both rows at a fixed 22 px pitch, a circular payload degrading to `[object Object]`, and a horizontal wheel leaving the scroll container at x=310. Then the overlay was changed: `truncatePayload` deleted in favour of `formatEventLogEntry`; one text object per event rendered with `lineSpacing: 2` and no `wordWrap`; row y offsets accumulate the measured text height + 6 px gap; `refresh(totalHeight, totalWidth)` now feeds both axes; `enableHorizontalScroll: true` is requested for this dialog only; the status line gains a 'scroll sideways for wide payloads' hint. Verified: browser suite 39/39 files green (73 s), `npm run build` clean.
